summary.text: The Berlin Wall was a guarded concrete barrier that encircled West Berlin from 1961 to 1989, separating it from East Berlin and East Germany.
East Germany's government began building it on 13 August 1961, with the main aim of stopping East German citizens from fleeing to the West.
It came down after East Germany announced on 9 November 1989 that its citizens could visit West Germany and West Berlin, paving the way for reunification.

facts.label: Departures beforehand
facts.value: 3.5 million East Germans defected before it rose

facts.label: Successful escapes
facts.value: Over 5,000 people got over the Wall

items.prompt: A government watches millions of its citizens cross a city border to settle in the rival half. What was the main purpose of the wall East Germany built?

options.label: To keep West German armies out of East Germany
To mark the edge of the Soviet occupation zone
To stop East German citizens from fleeing West
To stop West Berliners moving to the East

items.explain: Before the Wall, 3.5 million East Germans had left, and the primary intention of the Wall was to prevent such flight.

items.prompt: East Germany's official name for the Wall was the "Anti-Fascist Protection Rampart". What picture of the Wall did that name push?

options.label: A defence of the population against fascist plotters
An admission that it was built to keep people in
A temporary border post until Germany reunited
A memorial to the victims of the Second World War

items.explain: Soviet Bloc propaganda presented the Wall as protecting its people from fascist elements, even though its main aim was to stop people leaving.

items.prompt: About one in five East Germans left before 1961. Why did almost nobody manage it after the Wall went up?

options.label: Western countries stopped accepting newcomers
Travel by train between the zones was cheaper
Most East Germans no longer wanted to leave
Deadly force tied to the Wall stopped almost all

items.explain: After 1961 the deadly force associated with the Wall prevented almost all such emigration.

items.prompt: In November 1989 crowds of East Germans crossed and climbed onto the Wall. What had just happened?

options.label: The government announced that citizens could visit the West
Germany had formally reunified that same week
Demolition of the entire Wall had just been finished
The Warsaw Pact armies had been ordered home

items.explain: The East German government announced on 9 November 1989 that all citizens could visit West Germany and West Berlin; reunification came in October 1990.

items.prompt: The Soviets cut the land routes into West Berlin in 1948 so that food and supplies could not arrive. How did Western countries respond?

options.label: They invaded the Soviet zone to reopen the routes
They flew in food and supplies in a massive airlift
They paid the Soviets to lift the blockade
They moved West Berliners out of the city

items.explain: The US, UK, France and other countries ran a massive airlift supplying West Berlin until Stalin lifted the blockade in May 1949.

items.prompt: After the war, many people left the Soviet zone for the West through Berlin. What did this cost the Soviet zone?

options.label: Workers needed for rebuilding, especially educated people
Its factories, which were moved west by the Allies
Its ties to the Warsaw Pact military alliance
Its claim to be the legitimate power of all Germany

items.explain: The migration deprived the zone of workers needed for post-war reconstruction and disproportionately of highly educated people, the so-called Brain Drain.
